hawk: METR's open-source platform for running large-scale AI evaluations on AWS.
linuxarena: Redwood Research's AI control evaluation framework, benchmarking whether frontier monitors can detect a covertly misbehaving agent.
control tower: The core infrastructure harness Redwood uses to run evaluations across Dockerized environments.
A 2021 paper proposing a baseline template for visualization design guidelines, used here as the foundation this research builds on and extends.
modal: A serverless cloud platform for running GPU/CPU compute jobs without managing infrastructure.
supabase realtime: A Supabase feature that pushes live database updates to connected clients, used here to stream job status to the frontend.
claude api: Anthropic's API for accessing Claude models programmatically, used here to generate and grade interview questions.
flan-t5: An instruction-tuned language model from Google, used here as the base model for stance classification.
lora: Low-Rank Adaptation — a technique for fine-tuning large models by training small additional weight matrices instead of the full model, drastically reducing compute and memory needs.
mediapipe: Google's framework for real-time hand, face, and body tracking from camera input, used here to recognize hand gestures.
